question: The sixteen alert icons under the top bar: each one's condition, tooltip and click, the gates on the whole pass, the order they come up in and how icons are placed and removed.

addresses.name: CAlertManager_Update
addresses.revises: Read whole: every alert's test, every text, the order of the tests and the real extent of the scenario gate; the earlier entry had only the head and the decisions part and said every alert's flag was forced off in a scenario, which is wrong for 11, 14 and 15.
addresses.comment:
**The alert pass**, rva 0x201DE0 to the one `ret 4` at 0x206ED0. Called every frame from CInGameIdler_UpdateOpenView (0x251D30) unless the custom-game flag (the byte GetCustomGameSettings answers) is set. Each frame: the window of every alert up (+0x2C + n*0x88, window byte +0x5B set) is raised (slot 11) - that is what keeps icons on top. Then a gate: nothing more while the platform clock's seconds (+0xA0C, g_PlatformClock, slot 5) are below +0x8A0, or byte +0 is set (nothing in the image sets it to non-zero: the only write is 0 from CInGameIdler::OpenCountryView, 9 hits of displacement +0x1D28). Otherwise +0x8A0 = now + 3.0, so **the tests run at most once every 3.0 real seconds**, paused or not, and whatever the open country view.

The played country is gamestate->player. Local `noAlerts = gamestate->scenario (+0xD0C) != 0` forces the flag of alerts 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 13 false; **11, 14 and 15 have no such gate** (0x606AxC.. the reads of [esp+0xF] are at 0x60214A, 0x603C96, 0x604436, 0x6048D8, 0x604EF0, 0x6054D9, 0x605665, 0x605B26, 0x6061B6, 0x606770, 0x606AFE, 0x606E2D - and none before 11, 14 or 15).

The alerts are tested in this order: 0 NAP expiry, 1 deployable units, 2 troops in foreign territory, 3 revolt risk (built, hidden, never shown), 4 can invite to faction, 5 resource panic, 6 possible law, 7 free tech slots, 8 wasted IC, 9 tech far ahead, 10 lack of troops, 11 bad supply, 13 mobilised in peace, 15 allied objectives, 14 victory conditions, 12 national decisions. Each is shown (CAlertManager_Show) when its flag is true and it has no window, hidden (CAlertManager_Hide) when its flag is false and it has one; the texts are rebuilt inside this function per alert, or in the refresh helpers. **Whether an icon appears first depends on when its test first holds, not on its number.** See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-alerts.md for each alert's formula.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole on a throwaway copy of the project and read against the listing for every branch this entry states: the 3.0 double at 0x160A4E8, the twelve [esp+0xF] reads, the fifteen pushes before calls of 0x607FE0 (0, 1, 2, 4..15, none of 3), the calls of 0x608730. Shown wrong if an alert is found showing in a scenario other than 11, 14, 15, or a push of 3 before CAlertManager_Show.

addresses.name: CAlertManager_Show
addresses.revises: Read whole; adds the 30-second field nothing reads, the initial tooltip fill for alerts 4, 2 and 12, the register convention, and raises the confidence.
addresses.comment:
**Puts an alert's icon on screen.** Makes an `alerticon_window` through manager +0x14's slot 11 under the in-game screen's interface root, shows it (window +0x18's slot 13, window slot 11), sets the window's `alert_scope` (its +0x18's slot 30), sets `alerticon` to frame number + 1 and `alerticon_banner` to frame 0, hooks `alerticon` to the manager's observer +0x8A4, and places the window at the next place (+8, +0xC) through slot 42. Records x and y (+0x24, +0x28 of the record's block), writes clock + 30.0 into the record's banner_until (nothing reads it), and advances +8 by +0x10 (`alerticon_offset`'s x). Plays the `message` sound (sound manager slots 26 and 25 asked first, slot 9 plays; their exact meaning not read). Then number 4 fills its tooltip through CAlertManager_SetInviteTooltip, and 2, 3 and 12 through CAlertManager_SetTooltipList from the manager's scratch text (+0x9F0).

A caller passes the number on the stack and the manager in EDI: `push n; mov edi, esi; call`. Two `ret 4` at 0x608336 and 0x60837F. `alerticon_banner` is at x=5000 in the file (`#remove!`) and is never updated afterwards.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole; the call shape read at 0x603C6A and 0x604177, the double 30.0 at 0x160A8F0. Shown wrong by a reader of the record's +0x20 among the only code that holds the manager pointer, which is reached by displacement +0x1D28 only.

addresses.name: CAlertManager_Hide
addresses.comment: **Takes an alert off the row.** The record's window is destroyed through +0x18's slots 14 and 12, its pointer zeroed; then every other alert's window whose x stands to the right of this one's has its x moved left by +0x10 and is placed again (slot 42); finally the next place +8 is moved back by +0x10. So the row always closes up and order of arrival is kept. `ret 4` at 0x6087B2.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the loop's record stride 0x88 and the comparison on +0x24 read. Shown wrong if the x of a window is left alone by a hide.

addresses.name: CAlertManager_SetTooltipList
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CAlertManager_SetTooltipList(int number@ECX, CAlertManager* manager@stack:4, Hoi3CString* list@stack:8)
addresses.comment: Rewrites an alert's delayed tooltip text (the record's text at +0x4C of its block): GetText(`<name>_delayed`), with $LIST$ replaced by the given string, rendered in the settings' colours. Called for 1, 2, 3 (never in practice), 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12. `ret 8` at 0x608728.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the key `_delayed`, the substitution LIST and the store at the record's +0x4C.

addresses.name: CAlertManager_SetInviteTooltip
addresses.comment: CAlertManager_SetTooltipList's twin for alert 4: $LIST$ is FormatCountryTagList of the manager's tag list (+0x910, from number + 0x8D). `ret 4` at 0x608576.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the list argument and the `_delayed` key read.

addresses.name: CAlertManager_AlliedObjectivesTooltip
addresses.comment: **Alert 15's tooltip, whole.** `text` = AO_ALERT '§GAllied Objectives§W'. `delayed` is built over the played country's records in gamestate->+0xB9C[player]: for each record, the requesters' names (§Y name §W, ', ' between, ' ' + AND + ' ' before the last), OL_AO_THEY_REQUEST ' have requested that we', then OL_AO_DEFEND ' §Gdefend§W near ' when the province's controller's faction equals the player's, else OL_AO_ATTACK ' §Rattack§W near ', then '§Y' province name '§W.', with a newline between records. 0x6070D0 to `ret 4` at 0x60796C.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole; the strings and the literal byte sequences at 0x15B5C54 ('§Y'), 0x15B6700 ('§W') and 0x15BE90C ('§W.') read.

addresses.name: FormatCountryTagList
addresses.comment: A list of country tags as text, for the faction invite alert: each as `<name> (@<tag>)`, ', ' between while two or more remain and ' ' + AND before the last. The node is a tag and id with next at +0xC. Bare `ret`. Beside FormatProvinceList.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the strings ' (@', ')', ', ' and the AND key read.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OnAlertClicked
addresses.revises: Read whole: every arm. 'Only that arm was read; the function goes on through the other alerts' is replaced by the whole list, and alerts 0, 2, 3, 5, 13 and 15 are found to have no arm at all.
addresses.comment:
**Slot 80: what a click on an alert does**, by the alert's name, 0x64ACB0 to `ret 4` at 0x64B2CD (slot 81 at the next byte - trap 2). First, CInGameIdler_CloseSideMenus and CloseOrdersView, and the order of battle browser's open state (+0x1360 window +0xF4) noted; for `alert_deployable_units` the first selected unit (selection slot 1 answers 0, 1 or 2) is remembered; the selection is then cleared (Selection_Clear) **unless the alert is `alert_bad_supply` or `alert_lack_of_troops`**.

- `alert_deployable_units`: any open country view is closed (OpenCountryView(open_view), the toggle), then CInGameIdler_OpenSideMenu(5), the deploy menu; the remembered unit is reselected when Selection_CanAdd allows, and if the browser was open and the opening closed it, slot 104 opens it again.
- `alert_national_decisions`, `alert_can_invite_to_faction`: OpenCountryView(0), diplomacy.
- `alert_wasted_ic`: OpenCountryView(1), production.
- `alert_free_tech_slots`, `alert_tech_far_ahead`: OpenCountryView(2), technology.
- `alert_possible_law`: OpenCountryView(3), politics.
- `alert_lack_of_troops`: cycles through the player's units from the one after the first unit row's (unit_rows[0]+0x28), wrapping once, testing a unit with the alert's own test less the +0x40/first-brigade part; the first that passes is selected alone (ClearSelection, Select) and the map centred on its province (CentreOnProvince, slot 48).
- `alert_bad_supply`: the same cycle, testing supply_received_percentage < 1000 and nothing else.
- `alert_victory_conditions`: CInGameIdler::ToggleGoals only when the goals window is hidden.

**`alert_nap_expiry`, `alert_troops_in_foreign_territory`, `alert_revoltrisk_in_provinces`, `alert_resource_panic`, `alert_mobilized_in_peace` and `alert_allied_objectives` have no arm**: a click closes the side menus and the orders view, clears the selection and does nothing else. OpenCountryView is a toggle, so a click on an alert whose view is already open closes it. Reached through CAlertManager::OnIconClicked, which asks slot 69 first (true, unless the session object +0x1CD0 exists and its +0xF5 is clear).
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole, the string comparisons and the slot numbers read; slot 80 and slot 69 read out of the table at 0x15CEB54. Shown wrong by an arm for one of the six names listed as having none.

addresses.name: CAlertManager::OnIconClicked
addresses.revises: Adds the gate: the handler does nothing unless the in-game screen's slot 69 answers true.
addresses.comment: Finds which of the sixteen alerts a clicked icon is - by its frame less one, or by being that alert's banner - and hands the alert's name to the in-game screen's slot 80, all gated on the screen's slot 69 (0x678890: true unless the session object at +0x1CD0 exists and its +0xF5 is clear, so always true in a single-player game). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-alerts.md.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; slot 0x114/4 = 69 and its body read.

structs.name: CAlertRecord
structs.comment: One alert of CAlertManager's sixteen: its position, window, tooltip text and name.
structs.evidence: The eh vector constructor call in CAlertManager's constructor gives 0x88 x 16 at +0x20; Register, Show, Hide and IconTooltip each index it with the same stride.

structs.name: CAlertManager
structs.comment: The row of alert icons under the top bar. No RTTI of its own; the in-game screen holds it at +0x1D28.
structs.evidence: Built in CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x649398 and stored at +0x1D28 (0x6493AA); its fields read off the constructor, Show, Hide, Register and the update.

struct_fields.name: banner_until
struct_fields.comment: Show writes clock + 30.0 here; nothing reads it. The banner it presumably timed is off-screen and never changes frame.
struct_fields.evidence: Every path to a CAlertManager goes through the nine +0x1D28 sites, none of which touches a record's first dword; the reads of +0x2C and +0x24 show the same search does see the record's other fields.

struct_fields.name: x
struct_fields.comment: The icon's place along the row.
struct_fields.evidence: Show writes it from the next place; Hide compares and rewrites it.

struct_fields.name: y
struct_fields.comment: The icon's height.
struct_fields.evidence: Show writes it from the row's y.

struct_fields.name: window
struct_fields.comment: The `alerticon_window`, null while the alert is not up.
struct_fields.evidence: Show writes it; every alert in the update tests it to decide Show or Hide.

struct_fields.name: tooltip
struct_fields.comment: `_instant` in its text and `_delayed` in its delayed half, or the list the update built.
struct_fields.evidence: CAlertManager_Register writes +0x30 and +0x4C of the manager; IconTooltip copies a GuiTooltipText from the record.

struct_fields.name: name
struct_fields.comment: The alert's name, handed to the in-game screen when its icon is clicked.
struct_fields.evidence: Register stores it at manager +0x8C + n*0x88; OnIconClicked passes it to slot 80.

struct_fields.name: stopped
struct_fields.comment: Stops the alert pass where set. The only writes in the image are 0: the constructor and CInGameIdler::OpenCountryView (0x665967). So it never stops anything.
struct_fields.evidence: Displacement +0x1D28 has nine hits in .text; with the constructor and destructor that is every holder of the manager pointer. Shown wrong by a write through a copy of the pointer.

struct_fields.name: first_x
struct_fields.comment: The x of the first place: alerticon_startposition's x, plus alerticon_mp_offset's x in a multiplayer game (CInGameIdler +0x68). Not used again.
struct_fields.evidence: The constructor writes it and +8 from the same value.

struct_fields.name: next_x
struct_fields.comment: The next place: where the next alert to come up goes.
struct_fields.evidence: Show reads and advances it; Hide moves it back.

struct_fields.name: row_y
struct_fields.comment: alerticon_startposition's y.
struct_fields.evidence: Set in the constructor, used by Show.

struct_fields.name: step_x
struct_fields.comment: alerticon_offset's x, the distance between icons.
struct_fields.evidence: The constructor; Show and Hide both use it.

struct_fields.name: gui
struct_fields.comment: The interface object that makes `alerticon_window` (slot 11) and resolves the positionTypes (slot 18). The in-game screen's +0x60.
struct_fields.evidence: The constructor call at 0x649398 and the slot calls in the constructor and Show.

struct_fields.name: screen
struct_fields.comment: The in-game screen; OnIconClicked calls its slot 69 and slot 80.
struct_fields.evidence: OnIconClicked.

struct_fields.name: alerts
struct_fields.comment: The sixteen alerts, by number.
struct_fields.evidence: The constructor's vector construction at 0x88 x 16.

struct_fields.name: next_pass
struct_fields.comment: The clock's seconds before which the pass does nothing; set to now + 3.0 each pass. Zeroed by the constructor.
struct_fields.evidence: The head of CAlertManager_Update; movss reads and writes at 0x601EF9 and 0x601F28.

struct_fields.name: invitable_first
struct_fields.comment: List of the country tags alert 4 offers (0x14-byte nodes); last at +0x914, count at +0x918.
struct_fields.evidence: The list building in the update and its reader CAlertManager_SetInviteTooltip.

struct_fields.name: naps_due_first
struct_fields.comment: Vector of the NAPs alert 0 lists, rebuilt each pass; end at +0x9D4.
struct_fields.evidence: The push in the alert 0 section of the update.

struct_fields.name: foreign_provinces_first
struct_fields.comment: List of the provinces alert 2 names, deduplicated; last +0x9E4, count +0x9E8.
struct_fields.evidence: The alert 2 walk in the update.

struct_fields.name: scratch_text
struct_fields.comment: The text each list-building alert writes for its $LIST$; cleared between alerts.
struct_fields.evidence: Every alert's body in the update appends to +0x9F0 and clears it next.

struct_fields.name: clock
struct_fields.comment: g_PlatformClock, a CHighPerfWinClock; slot 5 answers seconds.
struct_fields.evidence: The constructor copies 0x1A857E4; the record's g_PlatformClock entry names the class.

struct_fields.name: revolt_provinces
struct_fields.comment: An array sized to the province count that alert 3's pass fills and sorts; never shown.
struct_fields.evidence: Allocated in the constructor from the province vector's size; the AlertPass_RevoltRiskList entry.

struct_fields.name: deployments_hash
struct_fields.comment: Alert 1: the sum of each listed deployment's +0xC, compared with the last pass to decide a tooltip re-render.
struct_fields.evidence: The alert 1 section of the update writes it once a pass.

struct_fields.name: alert_manager
struct_fields.comment: The alert row, built in Enter and passed to CAlertManager_Update each frame.
struct_fields.evidence: The nine sites of displacement 0x1D28, the construction at 0x6493AA.
